sources.entry: Panoply - Free file tools that run on your computer: PDF, images, video and audio, OCR, ID photos, instant file search and a disk map. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/anzal1/panoply) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Panoply is an open-source, on-device file utility app for macOS, Windows and Linux that covers PDF, image, video, audio, OCR, ID photo and sharing tasks without uploading files.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a single app bundling about 31 tools: PDF merge, split, page organizing, compression and conversion; image convert, compress, resize, metadata stripping, background removal, object erasing, watermark removal and 4x upscaling; ID and passport photo presets with KB-size resizing; video and audio conversion, trimming, compression, audio extraction, loudness normalization and HDR to SDR; and text extraction from images and scanned PDFs (Apple Vision on macOS, on-device models elsewhere). A command bar opens from a hotkey and accepts dropped files or plain-language requests. It also includes LocalSend-style file sharing on the local network, a `panoply run` command-line interface, and an `panoply mcp` server for AI agents. Results are written as new files next to the originals, and Undo moves them to the Trash. Models that are not in the installer are downloaded only after the user presses Download.
use_cases: compress a PDF or make it smaller
make passport or visa photos at exact KB size
OCR a scanned PDF into a searchable one
send files to nearby devices on my network
use file tools from an AI agent such as Claude or Cursor
stack: ffmpeg (external, used by video tools on macOS)
notable: Runs fully on the local device; no account, telemetry or uploads, with model downloads gated behind explicit consent and SHA-256 checks
Command bar with a global hotkey that searches tools and understands plain-language requests
Every tool is also a CLI command and an MCP server tool for AI agents
Community tools are packaged as a manifest plus a WebAssembly file that runs without network access
Non-destructive: outputs are new files and Undo sends them to the Trash
caveats: Beta release (v0.3.0) that is not code signed or notarized, so macOS and Windows block the first start and need manual approval
Video tools on macOS require a separately installed ffmpeg
Some features are still CLI-only (sharing is available from the command line today), and some tools need models or engines downloaded separately
Performance figures are reported by the author on an Apple M5 Max
summary.license: MIT or Apache-2.0 (dual licensed, at your option)
